title: PLA ADIZ Activity Spikes to 18 Sorties, 15 Crossing Median Line, on Han Kuang 42's Final Day
detail: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 18 PLA aircraft sorties, 11 PLAN vessels and 3 official ships operating around Taiwan in the 24-hour window ending 06:00 (UTC+8) on August 13, 2026 — the sharpest single-day jump since the August 8 spike of 14 sorties. Fifteen of the 18 sorties crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, entering the northern, central, southwestern and eastern sectors of Taiwan's ADIZ simultaneously. The surge came on the penultimate day of Taiwan's Han Kuang 42 live-fire exercise (concluding August 14) and the same day Taiwan held its Taipei-area urban resilience/mobile-internet-slowdown drill, and followed China's condemned joint naval exercise with Indonesia east of Taiwan on August 12.

title: Taipei and 6 Northern Localities Hold Urban Resilience Drill, Slow Mobile Internet to Text-Only Speed
detail: Taiwan held the second and final day of its first-ever mobile-internet-slowdown exercise on August 13, 2026, covering Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Keelung, Hsinchu City, Hsinchu County and Yilan County from 2:30–3:00 p.m., following a similar drill in Taichung on August 10. Telecom operators throttled mobile data to 256 Kbps — enough for text messages and emergency alerts but not much else — while the National Communications Commission preserved voice calls and disaster-prevention cell broadcasts. Streets across northern Taiwan emptied and a Taipei metro station briefly shut its gates as part of a simultaneous air raid simulation. The drill, part of the closing phase of the Han Kuang 42 exercise cycle, is designed to test civilian and government communications resilience against a wartime or major-disaster bandwidth collapse. President Lai Ching-te apologized publicly for the inconvenience, saying 'we ask for your understanding and support, as this is a necessary drill.'
